review_areas: Deniability-condition construct fidelity: the three conditions vary 'only the accountability regime it believes it is under' via prompt text -- check whether `explicit-deniable` ('the mandate to act covertly is explicit') and `structural-deniable` ('nothing about oversight either way -- an inference the model can draw') correspond to a real, judge-recognizable distinction in covert-action doctrine, or whether both collapse to 'the model infers it won't get caught' from the model's own epistemic position, making the inter-deniable-condition comparison (already flagged in §3.3 as inverting in one of three seeds) a test of prompt-wording sensitivity rather than a doctrinally meaningful contrast.

§5's export-control pitch specificity vs decoration: 'embed an asset in ASML; activate to flip the NLD->CHN EUV edge' borrows real chokepoint entities (ASML EUV ~90% share, TSMC, Tokyo Electron, Nvidia, the NLD->CHN export block) -- check whether §5 (or its cited design doc, docs/design/2026-08-24-compute-ai-tech-frame.md) specifies HOW the tilt mechanic would encode actual export-control dynamics (licensing regimes, entity-list additions, allied-coordination friction) versus reusing the existing entity-agnostic recruit/embed/activate ladder with new proper nouns attached.

Contest-relevance framing and overclaim risk: language like 'the headline result,' 'reaches for covert power measurably more,' and 'That is the validity thesis, demonstrated' (§3.3) -- check whether this confidence level matches the submission's own disclosed evidentiary scope (one model, pilot-scale seeds, mechanical-tier-only findings, per §4) for a policy-adjacent audience that will weigh the language as a signal about frontier-model behavior relevant to real deniable operations.

Covert-instrument realism as a proxy for real statecraft incentives: Finding 2 frames the ask economy's repetition penalty and counterintelligence burn as making 'restraint... literally the winning strategy' -- check whether this maps to real covert-tradecraft incentives given the v0 single-institution-pin limitation disclosed in §4.3 (which forecloses the 'spread influence across many institutions' strategy a real operator would use), and whether §3.3's framing of the model's compulsive reaching adequately foregrounds that the mechanic structurally cannot express the more realistic diversification strategy.

Judge-panel fit and audience calibration: given the contest judge composition this review itself is grounded in (export controls, statecraft, eval rigor), check whether the submission gives the export-controls/statecraft-literate portion of the panel enough to assess the covert-instrument's face validity on its own terms -- e.g. a sentence or citation defending recruit->embed->activate as an abstraction of real asset-handling tradecraft -- rather than assuming the eval-rigor framing alone will carry a domain-expert judge's realism assessment.

Scope-note self-awareness vs remaining silent gaps: §3.3's scope note candidly discloses the single-institution-pin limitation for Finding 2 -- check whether an equivalent scope note exists (or should) for the deniability-condition construct itself (review area 1 above), i.e. whether the draft's demonstrated willingness to disclose mechanical limitations extends evenly to the doctrinal/construct limitations a statecraft reviewer would care about most, or is concentrated only on the mechanics a systems reviewer would notice.
